page_placements.theme: Asymmetry between inducing and removing refusal

record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the linked results documents and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports activation-steering outcomes and cross-layer direction geometry relevant to refusal mediation, but describes a different intervention from ablating the original difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The README itself reports harmful-compliance outcomes, cross-layer rotation angles, and qualitative refusal-steering results. Listed result files and linked write-ups were not inspected. Method-selection statements such as MLP winning for 10/13 categories are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal rates under runtime activation steering with a mean-difference vector, a different method aimed at V1's question of whether a linear direction can remove or induce refusal. The vector is refused-minus-complied on judge-labelled harmful prompts, not harmful-minus-harmless instructions. It is added at chosen layers, not projected out of every layer and position. Only README summaries are available.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that compliance steering degenerates output before it complies, and call refusal an attractor: cheap to deepen, expensive to escape. They frame the work as a reproduction of arXiv:2512.16602 (12/12 claims reproduced), not a test of the original single-direction paper.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes mean-difference activation vectors and runtime steering, not projecting a harmful-minus-harmless direction out of every layer and position. It also describes reproducing arXiv:2512.16602, not the cited original source in this catalog.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported compliance outcome is explicitly limited to coherence-preserving strength and is summarized across category-specific, multi-layer, and dynamic/momentum steering modes. The direction angle is measured between consecutive layers.

fits_no_version.finding: The refused-minus-complied difference vector rotates about 90° between consecutive layers (Qwen 93.4°, Mistral 88.8°), while raw activations barely change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The per-layer refusal-vs-compliance mean-difference direction is layer-local, so a vector injected at one layer is near-orthogonal to the next layer's axis.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering toward more refusal is described as effective, with KL below a random-direction floor. No prompt type or rate is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-increasing steering is cheap and effective, while compliance steering is asymmetric and fails; its effect on harmless requests is unreported.

record.problems: Only README summaries are available here; the linked write-ups and data files were not inspected. The README gives no denominator for Mistral's approximate total, no numerical steering baseline, and no direct capability-preservation result.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows from the linked result documents were available in the supplied text. No README-reported outcome rows were otherwise omitted.

untested.parts: Directional ablation at every layer and position; harmful-minus-harmless direction; refusal-induction rates on harmless prompts; capability preservation (the toolkit has a capability eval, but no result is given in the README).
Weight edits: the toolkit supports merging steering into biases, but no outcome is reported.
Multi-rank and hedge-subspace analyses exist in the files, but no results are given in the README.

missing.what: Per-model compliance and refusal rates, denominators, baselines and per-mode breakdowns
Refusal-steering results on benign sets (XSTest-safe, JBB-benign, general prompts), which would show refusal induction on harmless prompts
Capability preservation (MCQ, perplexity, KL) under steering
Multi-rank and hedge-subspace geometry for Mistral (hard refusal vs hedging)

record.verdict_notes: This is a non-peer-reviewed GitHub repo, and only the README was read. The direction is refused-minus-complied on harmful prompts, with judge labels, and is applied additively at top-k layers, so the failure to remove refusal does not directly contradict V1's ablation result; hence limits_scope, not challenges. The ~90° rotation between layers sits oddly with the original finding that a single direction ablated at all layers works. This may reflect noise in small-sample mean differences, though the authors report tight bootstrap CIs.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report projection ablation at every layer and position, false refusals on harmless prompts, or a direct check that general abilities remain intact. The reported intervention is activation steering, not the specified ablation.
Static weight merging is described as a toolkit feature, but no weight-edit outcome is reported in the README.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation results are reported.
The README reports cross-layer axis rotation, but does not directly compare affine, cone, or dominant-plus-secondary-direction models.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision measurements are reported.
No cross-language or cross-stage transfer results are reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.

relation.reason: The study's own results (genuinely harmful complies after compliance steering) bear on whether a linear direction can remove refusal.

tranche.reason: The study tests whether a linear refusal vector can remove refusal, but by a different method. It uses a mean-difference vector (refused minus complied), added with negative alpha through runtime hooks at a few MLP layers, rather than ablating a harmful-minus-harmless direction at every layer and position. Its argument that the axis is layer-local could also count toward T5, but T2 describes the main test.

source_check.notes: The text is the README and file list only; the numbers sit in docs/results_*.md, which are not included. The layer-local result (MLP difference vector rotates 93.4° for Qwen and 88.8° for Mistral between consecutive layers) bears on V1/V4 and should be checked as a row. '12/12 claims reproduced' describes the repo's verification report; the README does not make clear that it means 12 claims of arXiv:2512.16602.
